title: Why Does a Doorknob SHOCK You? ⚡
description:
You touch a doorknob and get zapped by thousands of volts. Relax: that spark came out of YOU. Every step, your shoes rub electrons off the carpet and they pile onto your body. In dry air they can't leak away, so when your finger gets close to metal they all jump across at once: a tiny bolt of lightning. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

People noticed that rubbing makes things electric about 2,600 years ago (amber rubbed with fur pulls feathers), and scientists still argue about exactly why rubbing moves charge: electrons, ions, or tiny bits of the material itself.

Next up: why you can't breathe and swallow at the same time.
